andrea.title: Industrial Design Engineer | FTTH network project design | Graphic design, UI, 3D | Illustration
andrea.context: Andrea worked with Miguel in the same team
andrea.text:
I had the opportunity to work alongside Miguel on a project where he was responsible for the entire development of a web platform, including more complex features such as an interactive map, profile creation and management, registrations and a member directory, among others. He also does very good work on optimising and adapting the interface design, achieving a much more intuitive, fluid and efficient user experience.
As part of the project, he was also responsible for developing the mobile apps for Android and iOS.

Beyond his technical skills, I would also highlight the way he works: he is resourceful, ingenious, committed and very hard-working. He always looks for solutions to problems and is able to find practical alternatives in complex situations.

The experience of working with him has been excellent and I would undoubtedly recommend him for any project that requires technical ability, initiative and commitment.

laia.title: Emotional intelligence and empathetic communication specialist for wellbeing. Ontological coach. I support individuals, schools (students, teachers and families), companies and organisations.
laia.context: Laia was a client of Miguel
laia.text:
I have had the privilege of working with Miguel on the creation of my professional website (www.laiabobe.com) and I could not be happier with the result.

From the very first moment he understood the essence of my project and captured what I wanted to convey with my personal brand. It was very important to me that the website reflected who I am and the way I work, and Miguel achieved this beyond my expectations.

Throughout the whole process he stood out for his professionalism, his ability to listen and his commitment. He didn't just build a website: he contributed ideas, took care of every detail and was very willing to make the necessary adjustments until the result fully matched what I had in mind. At all times I felt heard, supported and well advised.

The final result is not only a well-designed and functional website, but one I feel fully represented by.

I recommend Miguel to any person or company looking for a rigorous, creative, committed professional with great human quality. If I ever need to develop another web project, I will not hesitate to work with him again. It has been a real pleasure to work with him.

Faq.title: Frequently asked questions
Faq.subtitle: Everything clients usually ask before we start

pricing.q: How much does a project cost?
pricing.a: It depends on scope. I offer fixed-price projects for well-defined work and a weekly rate for ongoing development. The free 30-minute call is where we agree scope, timeline and price, so there are no surprises afterwards.

usuk.q: Do you work with clients in the US and the UK?
usuk.a: Yes. I work remotely with teams in the US and the UK. I'm based in Spain (CET), which gives full-day overlap with the UK and about four hours of overlap with US Eastern time.

availability.a: I'm available for new projects and take on a limited number of clients at a time. You get a reply within 24 hours on business days.

start.q: How do we start working together?
start.a: Book a free 30-minute call or send a message through the contact form. We talk about your goals and constraints, and I come back with a proposal covering scope, timeline and price.

codebase.q: Can you take over an existing codebase?
codebase.a: Yes. App rescue and scaling is one of my services: performance work, refactors, CI/CD and reliability for products that already have users.

ai.q: What does AI & LLM integration include?
ai.a: RAG pipelines, chatbots, automations and speech features connected to your product and your data, using OpenAI or Anthropic APIs with vector databases such as PGVector or Chroma.

stack.q: Which technologies do you work with?
stack.a: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, React Native, PostgreSQL and Python, delivered with Docker and CI/CD.

cragxchange.title: CragXchange — a global rock-climbing community platform
cragxchange.description: Full-stack and mobile development of CragXchange: interactive crag map, member profiles, a directory and native iOS and Android apps built with React, React Native, Node.js and PostgreSQL.
cragxchange.challenge: CragXchange set out to connect climbers worldwide, but a directory alone was not enough. Climbers needed to find crags on a map, keep their own profile up to date and reach the community from a phone as well as from a laptop.
cragxchange.approach: I built the web platform end-to-end with React, Node.js and PostgreSQL: an interactive crag map, registration and profile management, and a member directory. I then extended the same product to iOS and Android with React Native, so one codebase powers both apps.
cragxchange.outcome: Climbers can open the app, find a crag, see who is around and share their own routes, while the client keeps a single web platform and a pair of native apps to maintain.

bluecode.title: Bluecode — website for a software agency
bluecode.description: Frontend development with React and TypeScript for the Bluecode marketing site, presenting the agency's services and portfolio work.
bluecode.challenge: Bluecode needed a marketing site that presented its services and previous work clearly to prospective clients, without a heavy CMS or a long maintenance burden behind it.
bluecode.approach: I built the frontend in React with TypeScript, translating the design into reusable, strongly typed components and structuring the content so pages could be updated without touching the code.
bluecode.outcome: A fast, maintainable agency site the team can keep up to date themselves, presenting Bluecode's services and case studies to the companies that evaluate them.

lifonet.title: Lifonet — real-time waste collection tracking
lifonet.description: Waste management platform built with React and Node.js: users open containers and follow their collections in real time.
lifonet.challenge: Waste collection only works when operators and residents see the same state: which container is open, which collection is under way and what has already been emptied. That state changes constantly, out in the field.
lifonet.approach: As full-stack developer I built the platform with React and Node.js, wiring live events from the field into the interface so containers and collections update as they happen instead of on a schedule.
lifonet.outcome: Residents open containers and follow collections in real time, and the operator gets an accurate picture of the service without chasing phone calls or spreadsheets.

laiabobe.title: Laia Bobe — personal brand website
laiabobe.description: Personal brand website for an ontological coach and wellbeing specialist, built with React: a clear, simple and elegant online presence.
laiabobe.challenge: The website had to carry a personal brand built on listening and trust. It needed to feel clear, calm and credible, and to be simple enough to update without help.
laiabobe.approach: I built a clean React site with a simple structure — services, about and contact — and went through several rounds of feedback until the tone, the copy and the design matched the brand.
laiabobe.outcome: A site the client feels represented by: simple to navigate, quick on mobile and easy to extend as the practice grows.

agrovolt.title: Agrovolt — mobile app for sustainable farming
agrovolt.description: React Native mobile app for Agrovolt's solar energy and agri-tech platform, bringing sustainable farming tools to iOS and Android.
agrovolt.challenge: Agrovolt's platform combines solar energy and agri-tech, and its users need those features in the field: on a phone, outdoors and away from a desk.
agrovolt.approach: I developed the mobile app in React Native, reusing the platform's existing APIs so the app and the web product stay in sync and features ship to both stores at once.
agrovolt.outcome: A cross-platform iOS and Android app that puts Agrovolt's sustainable farming tools in the hands of users where the work actually happens.

legalpyme.title: LegalPyme — legal services platform for small businesses
legalpyme.description: Web and mobile platform for small businesses with document management and working-hours records, built with React, Node.js and PostgreSQL.
legalpyme.challenge: Small businesses have to manage legal documents and working-hours records, usually in spreadsheets or on paper, with no easy way to prove what happened and when.
legalpyme.approach: I built the platform full-stack with React, Node.js and PostgreSQL, covering document management and the working-hours register across web and mobile so both stay in the same source of truth.
legalpyme.outcome: SMEs manage documents and working hours in one place, with a reliable record they can go back to whenever they need it.
